entries.what: f_DM < 0.2 fixes a BAND rather than a number, Newton sits at its floor by construction, and the transport law is refused only below a derivable depth

findings.name: the ceiling f_DM < 0.2 puts on the boost

expect.because: the whole comparison is against this number, and it is a definition rather than a measurement — so getting it exactly right is the cheapest thing in the section and the one everything else is quoted against

expect.of: −5.1% — Newton is at the band's floor, so he is wrong by the band
expect.because: Newton predicts no boost at all, so his error IS the dark-matter fraction expressed as a velocity — which is the sense in which he sits at the bottom of the band by construction rather than by fitting well

expect.of: −10.6% — at the top of the band Newton is as wrong as the model is at the bottom
expect.because: which is the point: an upper limit cannot single out a winner, and the arc's own 'four of five overshoot' is an adjective

findings.name: g_N/a₀ at which the law breaches the ceiling

expect.of: 3.2 — above this depth the transport law is consistent with f_DM < 0.2
expect.because: this turns 'four of five overshoot' into a statement about a MEASURABLE property of each disc — its baryonic acceleration at one effective radius — rather than about a count of galaxies, and it is falsifiable per object

findings.note: a disc whose baryons give more than 3.2 a₀ at R_e is allowed; one below it is refused, whatever its redshift — a₀ is local, so nothing here moves with z

entries.what: the carriers slowing where they are thin gives Newton in one limit and a flat curve in the other, with MOND's interpolation derived and its scale a₀ = cH₀/2π rather than fitted

findings.name: worst relative residual of g = g_N(1 + a₀/g)

expect.of: 0 — the closed form IS the solution, over six decades
expect.because: MOND's simple interpolation function is normally chosen for its shape; here it is what the turnover condition solves to, so the claim that it is derived is an algebraic identity and is checkable as one

expect.of: 1 — the thin regime is a 1/r force, which is a FLAT rotation curve
expect.because: n ∝ √Φ/r is what flux conservation gives once v ∝ n, and a 1/r force is the whole of what dark matter is usually invoked to supply

expect.of: 1 — Newton, recovered where the medium is dense
expect.because: one rule has to give both limits or it is two rules with a switch, and the solar system is the dense one

findings.name: v⁴ across a factor of 16 in radius, max/min

expect.of: 1 — v⁴ = GM·a₀ independent of radius, which is Tully–Fisher
expect.because: the flat curve and the Tully–Fisher relation are the same statement, and getting both from the transport rule is what makes this not a fit

findings.name: a₀ = cH₀/2π at Planck's H₀ (m/s²)

expect.of: within a tenth of the measured 1.2e-10
expect.because: making space has a rate, that rate is H, and an acceleration built from it has nothing free in it — so this is a prediction rather than a fit, and it explains why a galaxy appears to know the age of the universe

findings.note: Riess' H₀ gives 1.129e-10, so the Hubble tension brackets -13.2% to -5.9% against the measured value

entries.what: a count, a signed sum and a signed vector sum are three readings of the same rays — and the bias is quantised by the cycle because a dwell is whole ticks

expect.of: DEG — a count, which cannot cancel and so has one sign
expect.because: gravity is this moment, and a quantity that only ever adds cannot be screened: there is no negative mass to put in the way of it

findings.name: q = ⟨s⟩ with opposite signs on opposite exits

expect.of: 0 — a signed sum cancels, which is why charge comes in two kinds
expect.because: the same rays that gave a count of 26 give a charge of nought, so the difference between gravity and charge is the MOMENT and not the mechanism

expect.of: 0 — charged but not sided: the exits come in ± pairs, so Σ d̂ is nought
expect.because: a magnet needs a SIDE, and a source whose signs alternate over exits has none however many rays it puts out

findings.name: |µ| for a genuinely sided source

expect.of: well above nought — + out of one half and − out of the other IS a side
expect.because: this is the only one of the three readings that can tell which way a source is pointing, and it is what the magnetic arc is about

findings.note: and its charge is exactly 0 — SIDED WITHOUT BEING CHARGED, which is what a magnet is, and is why a magnet is not an electric object

findings.name: values the bias P can take

expect.of: CYCLE + 1 — a dwell is whole ticks, so P is quantised
expect.because: a real-valued P silently rounds onto the tick grid, so two different settings produce the same run and the difference is not measurable

entries.what: E and B both go perpendicular to the propagation direction and to each other with |E|/|B| → 1, which is c̄ in these units — a transverse electromagnetic wave, and the near field is NOT transverse, which is the same crossover seen from a second side

findings.name: ∠(E, r̂) in the far zone

expect.of: 90 — TRANSVERSE
expect.because: the thing a scalar theory could not have. E goes perpendicular to the propagation direction, and it does so only in the FAR zone — the near field of a dipole has a radial component and should

findings.note: and 99.35° at R = 200, so it APPROACHES 90° rather than sitting there — the same near-to-far crossover radiation/deficit-carries-a-1-over-R measures as |S|/|S′|, seen from a second side

expect.of: 0 — B is transverse EVERYWHERE, near zone included
expect.because: B = ∇×A is perpendicular to the separation by construction, so unlike E it has no radial part to lose. The asymmetry between this row and the one above is what a near zone IS

expect.of: 0 — and perpendicular to each other
expect.because: the second half of transverse, and the one that makes it electromagnetic rather than merely a transverse oscillation of something

expect.of: 1 — which is c̄ in these units
expect.because: the ratio of the field magnitudes in a plane wave is the propagation speed, and this model's is one cell a tick BY CONSTRUCTION — so the row is a check that the wave the potentials produce travels at the speed the rays do, which it did not have to

expect.of: 1 — a 1/R field, which is radiation
expect.because: the amplitude falls as 1/R rather than 1/R², which is the same 1/R term radiation/deficit-carries-a-1-over-R finds in the gradient — arriving here as a property of the wave rather than of the potential it came from

findings.name: how far it moves over a 3× box and a 8× run
